Because somebody needed it. Somebody in every generation is Heman. And if every psalm ended in the sunrise — that person would read the Bible and conclude *this isn't for me. Everyone in here gets the turn. I don't.* Psalm 88 says: *you're in here too. Your night without a morning is in the canon. God kept it.*

And here's the other thing. Heman wrote it *to God*. Every line. *Lord — God who saves me*. He didn't stop talking. He didn't write a note and leave. He *addressed* the darkness *to the One he couldn't see*. The prayer with no answer is still a prayer. The dim eyes are still *turned toward* something.

That's faith at the bottom. Not the feeling. The *direction*.

And — one more. The heading says *Heman the Ezrahite*. 1 Chronicles 25 lists him — a temple musician. A *worship leader*. The man who wrote *darkness is my closest friend* — led singing in the house of God. He didn't get fired for this psalm. It got *added to the hymnal*.

You can lead worship from the bottom of the pit. He did.

Eighteen verses. No turn. Here's the shape: *God who saves me — I'm counted with the dead — You put me here — my friends recoil — I pray every day anyway — can dust praise You? — why? — I've been here since I was a kid — darkness is my closest friend.*

If that's you tonight — you don't have to fake the turn. He didn't. Say it to God anyway. Address the dark to Him. That's enough. That's *in the book*.

And read Psalm 89 tomorrow. Not tonight. Tomorrow.
psalms.notes: *Note on translation: v. 1 —* Elohei y'shuati *= God of my salvation — the only positive divine title in the psalm. v. 5 —* asher lo z'chartam od *= "whom You remember no more." v. 6 —* b'vor tachtiyot *= in the pit of the lowest places. v. 8 —* shitani to'evot lamo *= "You have made me an abomination to them." v. 11 —* avaddon *= Destruction/Abaddon — the realm of the dead. v. 12 —* eretz n'shiyah *= land of forgetfulness/oblivion. v. 15 —* mi-no'ar *= from youth. v. 18 —* m'yuda'ai machshach *= "my acquaintances — darkness" — the final word. Sheol/pit/Abaddon throughout = the grave, not hell. No* yirah*.*

psalms.title: PSALM 89 — Where Is the Promise?
psalms.body:
Psalm 88 was one man in the dark. Psalm 89 is the whole *covenant* in the dark. The promise to David — the throne forever — and the throne is *empty*.

But Ethan doesn't start there. He starts with thirty-seven verses of *how good the promise was*.

**"I will sing of the Lord's loyal-love forever. With my mouth I will make Your faithfulness known through all generations."**

*Forever. All generations.* Confident. The word *chesed* — loyal-love — shows up *seven times* in this psalm. And *emunah* — faithfulness — *seven* more. He's hammering the two things God can't fail at.

**"I will declare that Your loyal-love stands firm forever — that You've established Your faithfulness in heaven itself."**

Then — the promise. God speaking:

**"'I have made a covenant with My chosen one. I have sworn to David My servant: I will establish your line forever — and make your throne firm through all generations.'"**

*Forever. All generations.* Same words. God's promise using the same timeline as Ethan's praise.

Now — a hymn to God's power. Long, and gorgeous:

**"The heavens praise Your wonders, Lord — Your faithfulness too, in the assembly of the holy ones. Who in the skies above can compare with the Lord? Who is like the Lord among the heavenly beings? In the council of the holy ones God is greatly held in awe. He is more awesome than all who surround Him."**

*Awe. Awesome.* *Yirah* twice. The angels themselves — *in awe*. Not cowering. *Amazed*.

**"Lord God of Armies — who is like You? You are mighty, Lord — and Your faithfulness surrounds You. You rule over the surging sea. When its waves mount up — You still them. You crushed Rahab like one of the slain. With Your strong arm You scattered Your enemies."**

*Rahab.* Not the woman — the *chaos monster*. Psalm 74's Leviathan. God crushed the thing that threatened creation.

**"The heavens are Yours — and Yours also the earth. You founded the world and all that is in it. You created the north and the south. Tabor and Hermon sing for joy at Your name."**

*The mountains sing.* Psalm 65 — the hills wear joy.

**"Your arm is endowed with power. Your hand is strong. Your right hand exalted. Right-standing and justice are the foundation of Your throne. Loyal-love and faithfulness go before You."**

Psalm 85's four virtues — *loyal-love and faithfulness* walking ahead of God like heralds.

**"Happy are those who have learned to acclaim You — who walk in the light of Your presence, Lord. They rejoice in Your name all day long. They exult in Your right-standing. Because You are their glory and strength — and by Your favor You exalt our horn."**

*You exalt our horn.* Psalm 75 — the horns of the righteous lifted up.

Now — the covenant with David. In full. God speaking, at length:

**"'I have found David My servant. With My sacred oil I have anointed him. My hand will sustain him. Surely My arm will strengthen him. The enemy will not get the better of him. The wicked will not oppress him. I will crush his foes before him — and strike down his adversaries. My faithful love will be with him — and through My name his horn will be exalted.'"**

**"'I will set his hand over the sea — his right hand over the rivers. He will call out to Me: You are my Father — my God — the Rock my Savior. And I will appoint him My firstborn — the most exalted of the kings of the earth.'"**

*My Father.* *My firstborn.* The king as God's *son*. Psalm 2 — *You are My son.* Hebrews 1 picks this up for Christ.

**"'I will maintain My love to him forever — and My covenant with him will never fail. I will establish his line forever — his throne as long as the heavens endure.'"**

*Never fail. Forever. As long as the heavens.*

And then — God anticipates the *problem*:

**"'If his sons forsake My law and do not follow My statutes — if they violate My decrees and fail to keep My commands — I will punish their sin with the rod — their wrongdoing with flogging —'"**

*If they fail — I'll discipline.* God saw it coming. The sons *would* blow it.

**"'— but I will not take My love from him — nor will I ever betray My faithfulness. I will not violate My covenant — or alter what My lips have uttered.'"**

*But I will NOT take My love.* Even if they fail. *The covenant holds.* Discipline — yes. *Abandonment — never.*

**"'Once for all I have sworn by My holiness — and I will not lie to David — that his line will continue forever — and his throne endure before Me like the sun. It will be established forever like the moon — the faithful witness in the sky.'"**

*Like the sun. Like the moon.* Same as Psalm 72. *I will not lie to David.*

Thirty-seven verses. That's the promise. Unbreakable. Sworn on God's holiness. Sun and moon.

And then — verse 38:

**"But You have rejected. You have spurned. You have been very angry with Your anointed one."**

*But.* The word that's been the *turn toward hope* in fifty psalms — is now the turn toward *catastrophe*.

**"You have renounced the covenant with Your servant. You have defiled his crown in the dust."**

*Renounced the covenant.* Ethan says it. The thing God just swore He'd never do — *You did it.* The crown's in the *dirt*.

**"You have broken through all his walls — reduced his strongholds to ruins. All who pass by have plundered him. He has become the scorn of his neighbors."**

Psalm 80's vine with the walls broken down — but now it's the *king*.

**"You have exalted the right hand of his foes. You have made all his enemies rejoice. Indeed — You have turned back the edge of his sword — and have not supported him in battle."**

*You turned his sword.* God — fighting on the *other* side.

**"You have put an end to his splendor — and cast his throne to the ground. You have cut short the days of his youth. You have covered him with a mantle of shame."**

*Cast his throne to the ground.* The throne that was supposed to be *like the sun*.

This is 586 BC. Jerusalem burned. The last Davidic king — Zedekiah — blinded, chained, hauled to Babylon. His sons killed in front of him. The line that was supposed to last *forever* — apparently *over*.

Now — the questions:

**"How long, Lord? Will You hide Yourself forever? How long will Your wrath burn like fire?"**

*How long.* Psalm 13, 74, 79, 80, 82 — it's the question of Books Two and Three. Here it's about the *covenant itself*.

**"Remember how fleeting is my life. For what futility You have created all humanity! Who can live and not see death — or who can escape the power of the grave?"**

Psalm 39, Psalm 90 — *we're vapor*. He's saying: *we don't have forever to wait. If the promise is going to come true — it needs to be in a human lifetime.*

**"Master — where is Your former loyal-love — which in Your faithfulness You swore to David?"**

*Where is it.* Not "does it exist." *Where did it GO?* He believes in it. He just can't *find* it.

**"Remember, Master — how Your servant has been mocked — how I bear in my heart the taunts of all the nations — the taunts with which Your enemies, Lord, have mocked — with which they have mocked every step of Your anointed one."**

*Every step.* They followed the king to Babylon — jeering the whole way.

And then — the psalm stops. And the editors add the Book Three doxology:

**"Praise be to the Lord forever! Amen and amen."**

*Praise be to the Lord forever.* Right after *where is Your loyal-love?* No answer. Just — the blessing. Because that's what you say at the end of a book. Even a book that ends in the dark.

Fifty-two verses. Here's the shape: *I'll sing of Your loyal-love forever. You promised David — forever, sun and moon, I will not lie. Even if his sons fail — I won't take My love. — BUT You've thrown the crown in the dirt. You turned his sword. Where is the promise You swore? How long? — Praise be to the Lord forever. Amen.*

Here's what Ethan couldn't see: the promise didn't fail. It went *underground*. The throne stayed empty for six hundred years — and then a descendant of David was born in a stable in David's town. *I will not lie to David.* He didn't. It just took longer than a human lifetime — which was Ethan's exact fear.

So — when the promise looks broken and the crown's in the dirt: say *where is it*. Say *how long*. Then say *amen* anyway. The line isn't over. It's just not visible yet.

Book Three ends here. Book Four opens with Moses — before David, before the throne, before any of it — reminding you that God was home before there was a kingdom to lose.
psalms.notes: *Note on translation: v. 1, 2, 14, 24, 28, 33, 49 —* chesed *(loyal-love) — seven occurrences. v. 1, 2, 5, 8, 24, 33, 49 —* emunah *(faithfulness) — seven. v. 7 —* nora *=* yirah *= held in awe / awesome (x2) — the angels' response. v. 10 —* Rahav *= Rahab the chaos monster (not the woman of Joshua 2). v. 26 —* avi atah *= "You [are] my Father." v. 27 —* b'chor *= firstborn — cf. Col 1:15, Heb 1:6. v. 33 —* lo-afir me-imo *= "I will not remove from him." v. 35 —* im-l'David achazev *= "I will not lie to David." v. 39 —* ne'artah b'rit *= "You have renounced the covenant" — the accusation. v. 47 —* meh-chaled *= how fleeting. v. 49 —* ayeh chasadecha *= "where [are] Your loyal-loves?" v. 52 — Book Three doxology.*

psalms.title: PSALM 90 — Teach Us to Number Our Days
psalms.body:
Psalm 89 ended with the throne in the dirt. Book Four's editors answered with the oldest voice they had — *Moses*. Before David. Before kings. Before the temple. A man who spent forty years in a wilderness watching an entire generation die.

This is what he learned.

**"Master — You have been our dwelling place throughout all generations."**

*Dwelling place.* Not the temple — that didn't exist. Not the land — they hadn't entered it. *You.* God as the *home*. Before there was a home. After the home burned. *You've been the address.*

**"Before the mountains were born — before You brought forth the whole world — from everlasting to everlasting — You are God."**

*Before the mountains were born.* Mountains are the oldest thing anyone can see. And God's *older*. Psalm 89 was worried the promise was too old to still count. Moses says: *He's older than the mountains and He's still here.*

Now — the hard part. Moses on mortality:

**"You turn people back to dust — saying: 'Return to dust, you mortals.'"**

*Return to dust.* Genesis 3. Moses is quoting the curse. He watched it happen to a whole generation — the ones who wouldn't go into the land.

**"A thousand years in Your sight are like a day that has just gone by — or like a watch in the night."**

*A thousand years — one day.* Or less — *a watch in the night*. Three or four hours. That's a millennium to God. Which means the six hundred years the throne would be empty — *an afternoon*.

**"Yet You sweep people away in the sleep of death. They are like the new grass of the morning — though in the morning it springs up new — by evening it is dry and withered."**

*Morning grass.* Green at dawn. Brown by dinner. That's a human life against God's calendar. Not depressing — *clarifying*. You've got a day. Spend it right.

**"We are consumed by Your anger — and terrified by Your indignation. You have set our wrongdoing before You — our secret sins in the light of Your presence."**

*Secret sins in the light.* Psalm 19 — *hidden faults*. Nothing stays hidden in front of Him.

**"All our days pass away under Your wrath. We finish our years with a moan."**

*With a moan.* Moses doesn't soften it. Most lives end in a sigh, not a fanfare.

**"Our days may come to seventy years — or eighty, if our strength endures — yet the best of them are but trouble and sorrow — because they quickly pass — and we fly away."**

*Seventy. Eighty.* Moses lived to 120 — and he's telling you *you* won't. And even the *best* years — *trouble and sorrow*. He's not selling you a soft life. He's telling you the truth so you'll spend it well.

**"If only we knew the power of Your anger! Your wrath is as great as the awe that is Your due."**

*Awe.* *Yirah.* Even here — in the psalm about dying — the response to God's greatness is *awe*, not terror.

And then — the verse. The one the whole psalm was heading toward:

**"Teach us to number our days — so that we may gain a heart of wisdom."**

*Number our days.* Count them. Know how many you've got — roughly. Not to be morbid. *So that* — purpose clause — *we gain a heart of wisdom.* The person who knows they've got a limited number of days spends them differently than the person who thinks they've got forever.

*Teach us.* It has to be *taught*. It doesn't come naturally. Every human being's default setting is *I have time*. Moses is asking God to override the default.

That's the whole psalm in one line. *Count the days — get wise.*

Now — the turn. And after the dust and the grass and the seventy years, it's *tender*:

**"Relent, Lord! How long will it be? Have compassion on Your servants."**

*How long.* Moses asked it too. In the wilderness. The oldest question in the book.

**"Satisfy us in the morning with Your loyal-love — that we may sing for joy and be glad all our days."**

*In the morning.* The grass springs up in the morning. Moses wants the *loyal-love* to spring up with it. *Satisfy us* — Psalm 63's fat and marrow — *first thing*. So the day that ends in a sigh can *start* in a song.

**"Make us glad for as many days as You have afflicted us — for as many years as we have seen trouble."**

*As many days.* Moses is asking for the *math to balance*. Forty years in the wilderness — forty years of gladness to match. He's not asking to erase the hard years. He's asking for *equal time on the other side*.

**"May Your deeds be shown to Your servants — Your splendor to their children."**

*To their children.* Psalm 78 — the next generation. Moses knew he wouldn't enter the land. He's praying for the *kids* who would.

And the last verse — a builder's prayer:

**"May the favor of the Master our God rest on us. Establish the work of our hands for us — yes — establish the work of our hands."**

*Establish the work of our hands.* Twice. The one thing a person with seventy years wants: *let what I built LAST.* Let it not be grass. Let it not blow away when I do. Moses built a *nation* in a wilderness — and he's asking God to make it *stick*.

That's the answer to Psalm 89. *The throne's in the dirt? He's been the dwelling place since before the mountains. A thousand years is an afternoon. Count your days. Ask Him to establish the work. Then let the kids see what comes next.*

Seventeen verses. Here's the shape: *You've been home forever. We're morning grass. Seventy years — eighty if we're lucky — and they end in a sigh. Teach us to count them so we get wise. Satisfy us first thing in the morning. Balance the hard years with glad ones. Show the kids. Make what we built last.*

Count your days. Then go build something He'll establish.
psalms.notes: *Note on translation: v. 1 —* ma'on *= dwelling place, habitation, refuge. v. 2 —* b'terem harim yuladu *= "before mountains were born." v. 3 —* shuvu v'nei-adam *= "return, children of Adam" — Gen 3:19. v. 4 —* ashmurah va-lailah *= a watch in the night (3–4 hours). v. 5–6 —* ka-chatzir *= like grass. v. 10 —* shiv'im shanah *= seventy years;* sh'monim *= eighty. v. 11 —* u-ch'yir'atecha *=* yirah *= "and according to the awe [due] You." v. 12 —* limnot yameinu ken hoda *= "to number our days so teach [us]." v. 14 —* sab'enu va-boker *= satisfy us in the morning. v. 17 —* ma'aseh yadeinu kon'nehu *= "the work of our hands establish it" (x2).*

psalms.title: PSALM 91 — Under His Wings
psalms.body:
Psalm 90 said you're morning grass. Psalm 91 says where the grass can hide.

**"Whoever dwells in the shelter of the Most High — will rest in the shadow of the Almighty."**

*Dwells.* Lives there. Not visits. *Rests* — the Hebrew is *yitlonan* — spends the night. Overnight in the shadow. You don't run to a shelter in the morning. You *sleep* there.

**"I will say of the Lord: 'He is my refuge and my fortress — my God, in whom I trust.'"**

*I will say.* Out loud. The psalm's telling you to *declare* it — because the declaration is part of the dwelling.

**"Surely He will save you from the fowler's snare — and from the deadly pestilence."**

*The fowler.* The bird-trapper. Hidden nets, baited hooks. The dangers you don't see until you're in them. *And pestilence* — the dangers nobody can fight. Both covered.

**"He will cover you with His feathers — and under His wings you will find refuge. His faithfulness will be your shield and rampart."**

*Feathers.* Psalm 17, 36, 57, 61, 63 — the wings, again and again. But here it's *feathers* — the soft part. Not the armor of the wing. The *down*. The warmth against the skin. God as the mother bird — and you as the chick that can't see anything but feathers and dark and *safe*.

**"You will not fear the terror of night — nor the arrow that flies by day — nor the pestilence that stalks in the darkness — nor the plague that destroys at midday."**

*Night. Day. Darkness. Midday.* All four quarters of the clock. There's no hour that's not covered.

**"A thousand may fall at your side — ten thousand at your right hand — but it will not come near you."**

*A thousand. Ten thousand.* He's not saying the danger isn't real. People *are* falling. He's saying — *not you. Not here. Not under the feathers.*

**"You will only observe with your eyes — and see the punishment of the wicked."**

*Observe.* A spectator. Watching from the shelter.

**"If you say: 'The Lord is my refuge' — and you make the Most High your dwelling — no harm will overtake you. No disaster will come near your tent."**

*If you say.* The condition — again — is *saying it*. Making Him the *dwelling*. Not the emergency exit. The *home address*.

Now — the angels:

**"Because He will command His angels concerning you — to guard you in all your ways. They will lift you up in their hands — so that you will not strike your foot against a stone."**

*Command His angels.* Orders. Given. About *you*. Psalm 34 — *the angel camps around*. Here they're *assigned*.

*So you won't strike your foot.* This is the verse Satan quoted to Jesus in the wilderness. *Throw Yourself off the temple — it's written, the angels will catch You.* And Jesus said: *It's also written — don't put God to the test.* The promise is real. It's not a *stunt*. You don't jump to prove the feathers exist. You *dwell*. There's a difference — and Jesus drew it.

**"You will tread on the lion and the cobra. You will trample the great lion and the serpent."**

*Tread on.* Not avoid. *Step on.* The thing that hunts you becomes the thing under your foot. Luke 10 — *I've given you authority to trample snakes and scorpions.* Same image.

And now — God takes the microphone. First person. Last three verses:

**"'Because he loves Me — I will rescue him. I will protect him — because he acknowledges My name.'"**

*Because he loves Me.* Not "because he earned it." Not "because he's righteous." *Loves.* The Hebrew is *chashak* — to be attached, to cling with desire. The one who's *stuck on* God — God rescues.

*Acknowledges My name.* Knows it. Says it. Psalm 91:2 — *I will say*. The saying was the acknowledging.

**"'He will call on Me — and I will answer him. I will be with him in trouble. I will deliver him and honor him.'"**

*With him IN trouble.* Not "I'll keep him out of trouble." *IN* it. The shelter isn't a place trouble can't find. It's the place where God's *standing next to you* when it does.

**"'With long life I will satisfy him — and show him My salvation.'"**

*Satisfy.* Psalm 63, 90 — the fat-and-marrow word. *Long life* — and Psalm 90 just said seventy, eighty. So "long" isn't a number. It's *full*. A life you're *satisfied* with, whatever the count.

*Show him My salvation.* The last word. Not "give him." *Show.* Let him *see it*. Psalm 27 — *I'll see the goodness of the Lord in the land of the living.*

Sixteen verses. Here's the shape: *Sleep in the shadow. SAY He's your refuge. Feathers over you. Night, day, darkness, noon — all covered. Thousands fall — not you. Angels assigned. Step on the snake. And God says: because he loves Me — I'm with him IN trouble — I'll show him salvation.*

Soldiers have carried this psalm into every war since it was written. Plague victims prayed it. It's been folded in pockets and tattooed on arms.

Here's what it's actually for: *dwelling*. Not a magic shield. A *home address*. Under the feathers. Say it out loud. Sleep there. And when the trouble comes — He's *in* it with you.
psalms.notes: *Note on translation: v. 1 —* yoshev *= one dwelling;* yitlonan *= will lodge/spend the night. v. 4 —* b'evrato *= with His pinion/feather;* tachat k'nafav *= under His wings. v. 5 —* lo-tira *= you will not fear — ordinary dread, correctly rendered (not* yirah*). v. 11–12 — quoted by Satan in Matt 4:6 / Luke 4:10–11; Jesus responds with Deut 6:16. v. 13 —* shachal *= lion;* peten *= cobra;* tanin *= serpent/dragon — cf. Luke 10:19. v. 14 —* chashak *= to love, be attached to, cling with desire. v. 15 —* imo-anochi v'tzarah *= "with him [am] I in trouble." v. 16 —* orech yamim *= length of days;* asbi'ehu *= I will satisfy him.*

psalms.title: PSALM 92 — Still Bearing Fruit in Old Age
psalms.body:
This is the Sabbath psalm. The one for the day you *stop*. And it turns out that when you stop — you can finally see what God's been doing.

**"It is good to praise the Lord — and make music to Your name, Most High — proclaiming Your loyal-love in the morning — and Your faithfulness at night."**

*Good.* The Hebrew is *tov* — the Genesis 1 word. *And God saw that it was good.* Praise is *good* the way creation is good. It's the right shape for a thing to be.

*Morning — loyal-love. Night — faithfulness.* Bookend the day. Psalm 92 gives you the two things to say at the two ends.

**"— to the music of the ten-stringed lyre and the melody of the harp."**

Instruments. It's not a quiet Sabbath. It's a *musical* one.

**"Because You make me glad by Your deeds, Lord. I sing for joy at what Your hands have done."**

*What Your hands have done.* Sabbath is *looking back*. Six days You worked — now I *see* it. The rest isn't empty. It's *review*.

**"How great are Your works, Lord! How profound Your thoughts!"**

*Profound.* The Hebrew is *am'ku* — deep. Psalm 42 — *deep calls to deep*. God's *thinking* has a floor you can't reach.

Now — the fool. Because there's always the fool:

**"Senseless people don't know. Fools don't understand — that though the wicked spring up like grass — and all evildoers flourish — they will be destroyed forever."**

*Spring up like grass.* Psalm 90's morning grass. The wicked are *grass* — green fast, gone fast. The fool sees the green and thinks it's permanent. The Sabbath-keeper sees the *evening*.

**"But You, Lord — are exalted forever."**

*Forever.* Not grass.

**"Surely Your enemies, Lord — surely Your enemies will perish. All evildoers will be scattered."**

*Surely.* Twice. He's not guessing.

**"You have exalted my horn like that of a wild ox. Fine oils have been poured on me."**

*My horn.* Psalm 75, 89 — the horn lifted. *Oils poured* — the anointing. Honored guest treatment. Psalm 23's table.

**"My eyes have seen the defeat of my adversaries. My ears have heard the rout of my wicked foes."**

*Seen. Heard.* Not "believe it will happen." *Witnessed.*

And now — the trees. This is what the Sabbath psalm was building to:

**"The righteous will flourish like a palm tree. They will grow like a cedar of Lebanon."**

*A palm tree.* Straight up. Doesn't spread. Doesn't sprawl. Grows *toward* something. Bears fruit at the *top* — where you have to look up to see it. And it grows in the *desert*. Oasis tree. Water underneath nobody can see.

*A cedar of Lebanon.* Psalm 29 — the tree God's voice *breaks*. But here the righteous *are* the cedar. Huge. Slow. Centuries. The wicked are grass; the righteous are the tree the grass grows under.

**"Planted in the house of the Lord — they will flourish in the courts of our God."**

*Planted.* Psalm 1 — *a tree planted by streams*. Psalm 52 — *a green olive tree in the house of God*. Psalm 84 — the sparrow with the nest by the altar. The image keeps coming back: *rooted where God lives*.

And then — the verse. The one for everyone who's ever wondered if they've aged out:

**"They will still bear fruit in old age. They will stay fresh and green."**

*Still.* In old age. *Fruit.* Not "they'll be remembered fondly." *Fruit.* Actual production. At seventy, eighty — Psalm 90's numbers — the palm's still dropping dates and the cedar's still throwing shade.

*Fresh and green.* The Hebrew is *d'shenim v'ra'ananim* — fat and luxuriant. *Juicy.* Old and *juicy*. That's the promise.

Psalm 71 — the old man asking not to be thrown away. Psalm 92 is the answer: *you're a palm tree. You don't stop.* The grass gets old and dies. The tree gets old and gets *better*.

**"— proclaiming: 'The Lord is upright. He is my Rock — and there is no wickedness in Him.'"**

*Proclaiming.* The old trees *talk*. That's what the fruit is — testimony. The Hebrew word for "proclaim" is *l'hagid* — to declare, to tell. Psalm 71's transmission. The fruit of the eighty-year-old palm is *the story*.

*No wickedness in Him.* The last line. After the grass and the fools and the horn and the trees — the Sabbath conclusion: *He's straight. Nothing crooked in Him.* That's what you see when you stop working long enough to look.

Fifteen verses. Here's the shape: *It's GOOD to praise. Loyal-love in the morning, faithfulness at night. Look at what His hands did. The wicked are grass — the fool thinks grass is forever. You've lifted my horn. I've SEEN it. The righteous are palm and cedar — planted in His house. Still bearing fruit at eighty. Fat and juicy. Telling everyone: He's straight.*

Stop working. Look back. You're a tree, not grass. And the fruit doesn't quit.
psalms.notes: *Note on translation: heading —* shir l'yom ha-shabbat *= "a song for the Sabbath day" — unique. v. 1 —* tov *= good (Gen 1). v. 5 —* am'ku *= are deep. v. 7 —* k'mo esev *= like grass (cf. Ps 90:5–6). v. 12 —* ka-tamar *= like the palm/date tree;* k'erez ba-L'vanon *= like a cedar in Lebanon. v. 13 —* sh'tulim *= planted (cf. Ps 1:3). v. 14 —* od y'nuvun b'seivah *= "still they will bear fruit in gray-hairedness";* d'shenim v'ra'ananim *= fat and fresh/luxuriant. v. 15 —* l'hagid *= to declare/proclaim. No* yirah*.*

psalms.title: PSALM 93 — The Lord Reigns
psalms.body:
Book Three ended with the king's crown in the dirt. Book Four's answer, in three words:

**"The Lord reigns."**

*Malak YHWH.* He is King. Present tense. Not "will reign." Not "used to." *Reigns.* Right now. While the earthly throne sits empty.

That's the whole point of Psalms 93 through 99. Israel lost its king — and discovered it had never *needed* one. The real throne was never in Jerusalem. It was *above* it.

**"He is robed in majesty. The Lord is robed. He is armed with strength."**

*Robed.* Dressed. The Hebrew is *lavesh* — to put on clothing. God *wearing* majesty like a garment. Like a king getting dressed for the throne room. The clothes *are* Him — but the image is *deliberate*. He's *ready*.

**"Indeed — the world is established, firm and secure."**

*Established.* Psalm 96, Psalm 24 — the earth set on the waters. Because the King is on His throne — the *ground holds*. Psalm 82 said when the powerful fail, *the foundations shake*. Psalm 93 says when the *real* King reigns — *they don't*.

**"Your throne was established long ago. You are from all eternity."**

*Long ago.* Before David's throne. Before Psalm 89's promise. *From eternity.* Psalm 90 — *before the mountains were born*. The throne Ethan mourned was a *copy*. The original's been occupied since before there was a *before*.

Now — the sea:

**"The seas have lifted up, Lord — the seas have lifted up their voice — the seas have lifted up their pounding waves."**

*Three times.* *The seas have lifted up.* Rising, rising, rising. The Hebrew is *n'harot* — rivers, floods — the chaos waters. Psalm 74's Leviathan. Psalm 89's Rahab. The thing that threatens to swallow everything — *getting louder*.

That's the sound of 586 BC. Babylon's army. The world coming apart. The waves *roaring*.

**"Mightier than the thunder of the great waters — mightier than the breakers of the sea — the Lord on high is mighty."**

*Mightier.* The waves lift their voice. The Lord is *louder*. Not by a little. Psalm 29 — *the voice of the Lord is over the waters*. The chaos makes noise. The King makes *more*.

You don't have to silence the waves. You have to hear what's *above* them.

**"Your statutes, Lord, stand firm. Holiness adorns Your house for endless days."**

*Your statutes stand firm.* The waves rise and fall. The *word* doesn't move. Psalm 12 — *silver refined seven times*. Psalm 19 — *the instruction of the Lord is complete*. When everything's water — the *word* is the rock.

*Holiness adorns Your house.* The temple burned. But *His* house — the real one — is still *decorated*. Still holy. Still standing. *For endless days.*

Five verses. Here's the shape: *The Lord REIGNS. He's dressed for it. The world holds because He's on the throne. That throne's older than the mountains. The seas are rising — three times — roaring. He's LOUDER. His word stands. His house is holy forever.*

When the earthly throne goes empty — when the leader fails, the institution collapses, the thing you trusted turns out to be grass — say the three words. *The Lord reigns.* He's been dressed for it since before the floods started.
psalms.notes: *Note on translation: v. 1 —* YHWH malach *= "YHWH reigns / has become king" — the enthronement formula (cf. 96:10, 97:1, 99:1);* ge'ut lavesh *= "majesty He has put on." v. 2 —* nachon kis'acha me'az *= "established [is] Your throne from then/of old." v. 3 —* nas'u n'harot *= "the floods/rivers have lifted up" (x3) — chaos waters. v. 4 —* mi-kolot mayim rabbim *= "than the voices of many waters";* adir ba-marom YHWH *= "mighty on high [is] YHWH." v. 5 —* edotecha ne'emnu m'od *= "Your testimonies are very sure." No* yirah*.*

psalms.title: PSALM 94 — Does He Who Made the Ear Not Hear?
psalms.body:
Psalm 93 said *the Lord reigns*. Psalm 94 says — *then why are the wicked still running things?* It's the right question. And the psalm answers it.

**"Lord — God who avenges — God who avenges — shine forth."**

*God who avenges.* Twice. The Hebrew is *El n'kamot* — God of vengeances. Not our vengeance. *His.* Romans 12 — *vengeance is Mine, says the Lord.* The psalmist isn't asking for permission to hit back. He's asking the *One who owns vengeance* to show up.

**"Rise up, Judge of the earth. Pay back to the proud what they deserve."**

**"How long, Lord, will the wicked — how long will the wicked be jubilant?"**

*Jubilant.* Not just winning — *celebrating*. Throwing the party. Psalm 73's wicked with the fans. *How long* — the question again — but now specifically about the *gloating*.

**"They pour out arrogant words. All the evildoers are full of boasting. They crush Your people, Lord. They oppress Your inheritance."**

*Your* people. *Your* inheritance. Asaph's move — make it God's problem.

**"They slay the widow and the foreigner. They murder the fatherless."**

The three groups every law in Torah protected — *widow, foreigner, orphan*. Exodus 22, Deuteronomy 10, 24, 27. The people with no one. And the wicked went straight for them. That's not random cruelty. That's *targeting*.

**"They say: 'The Lord does not see. The God of Jacob pays no heed.'"**

Psalm 10, 14, 59, 64 — *who sees? who hears?* The oppressor's working assumption. *No one's watching.*

And now — the psalm turns and *argues* with them. And it's one of the sharpest arguments in the book:

**"Take notice, you senseless ones among the people. You fools — when will you become wise?"**

**"Does He who fashioned the ear not hear? Does He who formed the eye not see?"**

Stop and think about that.

*He MADE the ear.* Designed the eardrum, the tiny bones, the nerve that turns vibration into meaning. And you think He's *deaf*?

*He FORMED the eye.* The lens, the retina, the rods and cones, the whole miracle of light becoming sight. And you think He's *blind*?

The argument is: *the Maker of the sense has the sense.* You can't build a thing you don't understand. The One who invented hearing *hears*. The One who invented seeing *sees*. The oppressor's whole strategy — *nobody's watching* — collapses the moment you look at your own ear.

**"Does He who disciplines nations not punish? Does He who teaches mankind lack knowledge?"**

*He who teaches mankind.* Everything you know — He's the source of knowing. And you think He *doesn't know*?

**"The Lord knows all human plans. He knows that they are futile."**

*Futile.* The Hebrew is *hevel* — vapor. Psalm 39, 62. Every scheme of the wicked — *breath*. He's seen the whole plan and knows how it ends before it starts.

Now — the turn toward the reader:

**"Happy is the one You discipline, Lord — the one You teach from Your law."**

*Happy is the one You DISCIPLINE.* Read that again. The psalm's been about the wicked who get away with it. And it says — *you're the lucky one*. Because you're being *corrected*. They're not. Being disciplined means you're *in the family*. Hebrews 12 — *whom the Lord loves He disciplines*. The wicked's freedom from correction isn't a gift. It's *abandonment*.

**"You grant them relief from days of trouble — till a pit is dug for the wicked."**

*Till.* There's a *till*. Psalm 7's pit is being dug right now.

**"Because the Lord will not reject His people. He will never forsake His inheritance."**

*Never.* The word Psalm 89 was afraid of. *Never forsake.*

**"Judgment will again be founded on right-standing — and all the upright in heart will follow it."**

*Again.* Justice *comes back*. The courts get fixed. Not in theory — in the psalm's certainty.

Now — the personal testimony:

**"Who will rise up for me against the wicked? Who will take a stand for me against evildoers? Unless the Lord had given me help — I would soon have dwelt in the silence of death."**

*Unless.* One word between him and the grave. *Unless the Lord had helped.* No other explanation for why he's still breathing.

**"When I said: 'My foot is slipping' — Your loyal-love, Lord, supported me."**

*My foot is slipping.* Psalm 73 — *my feet almost stumbled*. Same edge. And — *loyal-love supported me*. He didn't catch himself. He was *caught*.

And then — the most tender verse in the psalm:

**"When anxiety was great within me — Your consolation brought me joy."**

*Anxiety.* The Hebrew is *sar'apai* — disquieting thoughts, the racing mind. The 3 a.m. loop. Psalm 77's insomnia.

*Your consolation.* The Hebrew is *tanchumecha* — Your *comforts*, plural. Not one big comfort. Many. Layered. The same root as Psalm 71's *nacham*.

*Brought me joy.* Not just quieted the anxiety. Turned it into *delight*. Psalm 30's *mourning into dancing*.

If you've got the racing mind — this verse. *When anxiety was great within me — Your comforts delighted me.*

**"Can a corrupt throne be allied with You — a throne that brings on misery by its decrees? The wicked band together against the righteous — and condemn the innocent to death."**

*A corrupt throne.* Psalm 82's gods. The judges who tilt the scales. *Allied with You?* No. God doesn't sit on that bench.

**"But the Lord has become my fortress — and my God the rock in whom I take refuge."**

**"He will repay them for their sins — and destroy them for their wickedness. The Lord our God will destroy them."**

*Our God.* Not "God in the abstract." *Ours.* The One who made the ear.

Twenty-three verses. Here's the shape: *God of vengeance — shine. How long will the wicked GLOAT? They murder the widow and the orphan and say no one sees. — He MADE the ear. He FORMED the eye. — Happy is the one He disciplines — that means you're His. He'll never forsake. My foot slipped — He caught me. My mind raced — His comforts delighted me. The corrupt throne isn't His. He's my fortress.*

When they say nobody's watching: look at your own ear. He built it. He's listening.
psalms.notes: *Note on translation: v. 1 —* El-n'kamot *= God of vengeances (x2). v. 3 —* ya'alozu *= exult, be jubilant. v. 6 —* almanah, ger, y'tomim *= widow, foreigner, orphans — the protected classes of Torah. v. 9 —* ha-nota ozen ha-lo yishma *= "the planter of the ear — will He not hear?";* yotzer ayin *= the former of the eye. v. 11 —* hevel *= vapor, futile. v. 12 —* ashrei ha-gever asher-t'yas'renu *= "happy [is] the man whom You discipline." v. 17 —* lulei YHWH *= "unless YHWH";* dumah *= silence (of death). v. 19 —* sar'apai *= my anxious/divided thoughts;* tanchumecha *= Your comforts (pl.);* y'sha'ash'u nafshi *= delight my soul. No* yirah*.*

psalms.title: PSALM 95 — Today, If You Hear His Voice
psalms.body:
Half invitation. Half alarm. And the hinge is one word.

**"Come — let us sing for joy to the Lord! Let us shout aloud to the Rock of our salvation!"**

*Come.* Plural. *Let us.* This isn't a private psalm. It's a *summons* — somebody standing at the temple gate calling the crowd in.

**"Let us come before Him with thanksgiving — and extol Him with music and song."**

*Thanksgiving first.* Psalm 50 — *offer God thanksgiving*. Before you ask for anything — thank.

**"Because the Lord is the great God — the great King above all gods."**

*Above all gods.* Psalm 82's gods — the powers, the rulers, the things people bow to. *Above* them all. The enthronement theme continues.

**"In His hand are the depths of the earth — and the mountain peaks belong to Him. The sea is His — He made it — and His hands formed the dry land."**

*Depths and peaks.* The lowest and the highest — *in His hand*. *The sea* — the chaos — *His. He made it.* Psalm 93's roaring waves — *He built them*. You don't fear what you manufactured.

Now — the posture changes. From shouting to kneeling:

**"Come — let us bow down in worship. Let us kneel before the Lord our Maker."**

*Bow. Kneel.* The body goes down. After the shout — the *silence*. Both are worship. Psalm 47 said clap. Psalm 95 says kneel. You need both.

*Our Maker.* Not just the world's — *ours*. He formed the dry land and He formed *you*.

**"Because He is our God — and we are the people of His pasture — the flock under His care."**

*The flock under His care.* Psalm 23, 74, 79, 80 — *sheep*. Always sheep. Because sheep don't manage themselves.

And then — the hinge. The word Hebrews built two chapters on:

**"Today — if only you would hear His voice —"**

*Today.* *Ha-yom.* Not tomorrow. Not "when I've got things sorted." *Today.*

*If only you would hear.* Not "if He would speak." He's *speaking*. The question is whether you'll *hear*. Psalm 81 — *if only My people would listen*. The voice isn't the problem. The ear is.

Hebrews 3:7–4:11 quotes this and says: *the "today" is still open. As long as it's called "today" — you can still go in.* The door didn't close with Israel. It's *now*.

Now — the warning. God speaking:

**"'— do not harden your hearts as you did at Meribah — as you did that day at Massah in the wilderness — where your ancestors tested Me. They tried Me — though they had seen what I did.'"**

*Meribah. Massah.* Exodus 17, Numbers 20. The places Israel demanded water and said *is the Lord among us or not?* — *after* the sea split, *after* the manna fell. They'd *seen it*. And they still asked *is He even here?*

*Harden your hearts.* The Hebrew is *al-takshu* — don't make it *stiff*. The heart that's seen the miracle and still says *prove it* — that's not doubt. That's *hardness*. Doubt asks. Hardness *demands*.

**"'For forty years I was angry with that generation. I said: They are a people whose hearts go astray — and they have not known My ways.'"**

*Forty years.* An entire generation — the ones who came out of Egypt — wandered until they died. Psalm 90's Moses watched every funeral. *Their hearts went astray* — not their feet. The feet followed the cloud. The *hearts* wandered.

**"'So I declared on oath in My anger: They shall never enter My rest.'"**

*My rest.* The land. Canaan. The promise. They got *close* — Moses saw it from the mountain — and *didn't go in*. Not because God changed His mind. Because they *wouldn't trust Him for the next thing* after He'd done the last thing.

And here's Hebrews' point: *there's still a rest. Today. The door's open. Don't be the generation that saw everything and went in for nothing.*

Eleven verses. Here's the shape: *Come — shout. He's above all gods. He built the sea. Come — kneel. We're His sheep. TODAY — if you'd hear His voice — don't stiffen. They saw the miracles and still said "prove it." Forty years. They never entered. — You still can.*

*Today* is the only day you've ever been given. Hear the voice in it. Go in.
psalms.notes: *Note on translation: v. 1 —* l'chu n'ran'nah *= "come, let us sing" — plural imperative. v. 6 —* nishtachaveh v'nichra'ah *= let us bow down and kneel;* osenu *= our Maker. v. 7 —* tzon yado *= flock of His hand. v. 7 —* ha-yom im-b'kolo tishma'u *= "today, if His voice you would hear" — Hebrews 3:7, 15; 4:7. v. 8 —* al-takshu l'vavchem *= "do not harden your heart";* Merivah / Massah *= "contention / testing" — Exod 17:1–7, Num 20:1–13. v. 10 —* arba'im shanah *= forty years. v. 11 —* im-y'vo'un el-m'nuchati *= "[surely] they shall not enter My rest." No* yirah*.*

psalms.title: PSALM 96 — Sing a New Song
psalms.body:
Psalm 93 said *the Lord reigns*. Psalm 96 says — *so tell everybody. And get the trees involved.*

**"Sing to the Lord a new song! Sing to the Lord, all the earth!"**

*A new song.* Psalm 33, 40 — fresh material. Not because the old songs are bad. Because *He did something new* and it needs its own melody.

*All the earth.* Not Israel. *All.* Every continent's invited to the choir.

**"Sing to the Lord. Praise His name. Proclaim His salvation day after day."**

*Day after day.* Not once. A *rhythm*. Psalm 61 — *day by day I pay my vows*.

**"Declare His glory among the nations — His marvelous deeds among all peoples."**

*Among the nations.* You don't sing this one inside the temple with the doors closed. You take it *out*. To the people who've never heard the name.

**"Because great is the Lord — and most worthy of praise. He is to be held in awe above all gods."**

*Awe.* *Yirah* — *nora*. Above all gods. Not "feared." *Awe-inspiring beyond every rival.* The word the KJV rendered "feared" here, in the middle of a verse commanding *praise*.

**"Because all the gods of the nations are idols — but the Lord made the heavens."**

*Idols.* The Hebrew is *elilim* — a pun. *Elohim* means gods. *Elilim* means *nothings*. Worthless things. The nations' gods are *elilim* — *nothing-gods*. And the Lord *made the sky they're looking at*.

**"Splendor and majesty are before Him. Strength and glory are in His sanctuary."**

Now — the invitation to the nations. And it's *specific*:

**"Ascribe to the Lord, all you families of nations — ascribe to the Lord the glory due His name."**

*Families of nations.* Not governments. *Families.* Genesis 12 — *all the families of the earth will be blessed.* The invitation goes to the *household* level.

**"Bring an offering and come into His courts. Worship the Lord in the splendor of His holiness."**

*Come into His courts.* The foreigners — *inside*. Psalm 87 — *born in Zion*. The door's open to the families that used to be enemies.

**"Tremble before Him, all the earth!"**

*Tremble.* The Hebrew is *chilu* — writhe, shake, be moved. Psalm 2 — *rejoice with trembling*. It's not terror. It's the *physical response* to standing in front of something that big. Your knees do it on their own.

And now — the three words:

**"Say among the nations: 'The Lord reigns!'"**

*Say it among the nations.* Psalm 93's three words — carried *out*. To Babylon. To Egypt. To the places that have their own kings. *Yours isn't the real one. Here's Who is.*

**"The world is firmly established. It cannot be moved. He will judge the peoples with equity."**

*Cannot be moved.* Psalm 93 — *the world is established*. Psalm 15, 16, 21, 30 — *not shaken*. Because the King's on the throne.

*Equity.* Fairness. Psalm 82's failed gods tilted the scale. The real King judges *straight*.

And then — the whole creation joins in. Watch how it *spreads*:

**"Let the heavens rejoice! Let the earth be glad! Let the sea resound — and all that is in it! Let the fields be jubilant — and everything in them!"**

Heavens. Earth. Sea. Fields. Everything *in* them. The fish. The wheat. The whole thing *singing*.

**"Let all the trees of the forest sing for joy!"**

*The trees.* Every one. Psalm 92's palm and cedar. Psalm 1's tree by the water. Psalm 52's olive. Now the *whole forest* — every trunk and branch — *singing*. Isaiah 55 — *the trees of the field will clap their hands.* Paul in Romans 8 — *creation groans, waiting*. Psalm 96 says: *and then it SINGS.*

**"Let them sing before the Lord — because He comes — He comes to judge the earth."**

*He comes.* Twice. *He's coming.* Not to condemn — to *judge*. To *set things right*. To fix Psalm 82's courts. And the trees are *glad about it* — because when the Judge comes, the ones who've been crushed get lifted, and the creation that's been groaning gets *heard*.

**"He will judge the world in right-standing — and the peoples in His faithfulness."**

*Faithfulness.* The last word. The Judge is *faithful*. He doesn't rule by mood. He rules by *promise*. Psalm 89's seven *emunah*s — here's where they land.

Thirteen verses. Here's the shape: *New song — all the earth. Day after day. Among the NATIONS. He's awesome above the nothing-gods. Families — come in. Tremble. Say it out there: the Lord REIGNS. The world can't be moved. Heavens, earth, sea, fields — sing. TREES — sing. He's coming to set it right. Faithfully.*

Tell somebody who doesn't know. Then go outside and listen to the trees. They already do.
psalms.notes: *Note on translation: v. 1 —* shir chadash *= new song (cf. 33:3, 40:3). v. 4 —* nora hu al-kol-elohim *=* yirah *= "awesome [is] He above all gods" — KJV "to be feared." v. 5 —* elilim *= idols/worthless things — pun on* elohim*. v. 7 —* mishp'chot amim *= families of peoples (Gen 12:3, 28:14). v. 9 —* chilu mi-panav *= tremble/writhe before Him. v. 10 —* YHWH malach *= "YHWH reigns" (cf. 93:1). v. 12 —* kol-atzei-ya'ar *= all trees of the forest. v. 13 —* ki va ki va *= "for He comes, for He comes." Nearly identical to 1 Chronicles 16:23–33.*

psalms.title: PSALM 97 — Light Is Sown for the Righteous
psalms.body:
Psalm 96 said *He comes*. Psalm 97 shows you what it looks like when He does.

**"The Lord reigns! Let the earth be glad! Let the distant shores rejoice!"**

*The Lord reigns.* Third time — 93, 96, now 97. *Distant shores* — the Hebrew is *iyim rabbim* — the many islands. The far edges. The places that can barely see the mainland. *They* rejoice too.

**"Clouds and thick darkness surround Him. Right-standing and justice are the foundation of His throne."**

*Clouds and darkness.* Sinai. Exodus 19 — the mountain wrapped in smoke. Psalm 18 — *He made darkness His covering*. The King comes in *weather*. You can't see Him directly. You see the *cloud*.

And *under* the cloud — the throne. And under the throne — *right-standing and justice*. Not power. Not force. The foundation is *fairness*. Psalm 89:14 said the same. The thing holding up the King's chair is *doing right*.

**"Fire goes before Him — and consumes His foes on every side."**

*Fire goes before.* Psalm 50 — *fire devours in front of Him*. The herald is *flame*. Everything that opposed Him — gone before He even arrives.

**"His lightning lights up the world. The earth sees and trembles."**

*The earth sees.* Not just people. The *planet* watches. Psalm 96 — *tremble before Him, all the earth*. Here it *does*.

**"The mountains melt like wax before the Lord — before the Master of all the earth."**

*Melt like wax.* The most permanent thing in the landscape — *liquid*. Psalm 46 — *the mountains fall into the sea*. Psalm 68 — *wax melts before fire*. When the King shows up, the *geography* gives.

**"The heavens proclaim His right-standing — and all peoples see His glory."**

*All peoples see.* Not hear about. *See.* Psalm 98 will say the same. The vision of Book Four is *visible* — everyone on earth with their eyes on the same thing.

Now — the idols:

**"All who worship images are put to shame — those who boast in idols. Worship Him — all you gods!"**

*Worship Him — all you gods.* Psalm 96's *nothing-gods*. Psalm 82's failed rulers. Whatever they are — *they bow*. The King doesn't argue with rival gods. He *commands* them. And they kneel.

If there's something you've been bowing to — money, approval, the substance, the person — it's in this line. *Worship Him.* The command goes to the idol. It has to bow too.

**"Zion hears and rejoices. The villages of Judah are glad — because of Your judgments, Lord."**

*Because of Your judgments.* They're *glad* about the judging. Because the judgments are *fair* — and fair judgment is good news for the people who've been getting the short end.

**"Because You, Lord, are the Most High over all the earth. You are exalted far above all gods."**

Now — the turn from the storm to the *people*:

**"Let those who love the Lord hate evil."**

*Love — hate.* Both. You can't love the King and be neutral about what He's against. Psalm 45 — *You've loved right-standing and hated wickedness*. If you love the one, you *hate* the other. Not the *people* — the *evil*. The thing that crushes them.

**"He guards the lives of His faithful ones — and delivers them from the hand of the wicked."**

*Guards. Delivers.* Psalm 91's shelter. Psalm 121's keeper. Same promise in the middle of the storm.

And then — the verse. The strangest and most beautiful image in the enthronement psalms:

**"Light is sown for the righteous — and joy for the upright in heart."**

*Light is SOWN.*

Read it again. *Sown.* Like seed. Like a farmer walking a field with a bag, scattering. But he's not scattering grain — he's scattering *light*. Into the dirt. Into the dark ground. Where you can't see it yet.

And what happens to seed? It goes *under*. It disappears. For a while, the field looks *empty*. Then — it comes *up*.

That's what God's doing for the righteous. *Sowing light.* You're standing in a dark field and it looks like nothing. But there's light *under the soil*. Planted. Germinating. And it's going to break the surface.

Psalm 88 — *darkness is my closest friend*. Psalm 97 — *light is sown for the righteous*. Same dark field. But the light's already in the ground.

*And joy.* Sown too. Coming up with it.

**"Rejoice in the Lord, you who are righteous — and praise His holy name."**

*Rejoice.* Because the seed's in. You just can't see it yet.

Twelve verses. Here's the shape: *The Lord reigns — even the islands rejoice. He comes in cloud and darkness — with justice under the throne. Fire ahead. Mountains melt. Everyone SEES. The idols bow — He commands them. Love Him, hate evil. He guards you. And — light is SOWN for you. It's in the ground. Rejoice.*

Your field looks dark? Check the soil. He's been planting.
psalms.notes: *Note on translation: v. 1 —* iyim rabbim *= many islands/coastlands. v. 2 —* anan va-arafel *= cloud and thick darkness (Exod 19:9, 16; Deut 4:11). v. 5 —* ka-donag namasu *= like wax they melted. v. 7 —* hishtachavu-lo kol-elohim *= "bow down to Him, all gods." v. 10 —* ohavei YHWH sin'u ra *= "lovers of YHWH — hate evil." v. 11 —* or zaru'a la-tzadik *= "light [is] sown for the righteous" — some MSS read* zarach *(dawns/rises); the Masoretic* zaru'a *(sown) is retained and is the richer image. No* yirah*.*

psalms.title: PSALM 98 — Let the Rivers Clap Their Hands
psalms.body:
Every December you sing this and don't know it. *Joy to the World* isn't from Luke. It's from Psalm 98.

**"Sing to the Lord a new song — because He has done marvelous things. His right hand and His holy arm have worked salvation for Him."**

*A new song.* Third time in Book Four. Because *He did something* — the Hebrew is *nifla'ot*, wonders — and the old song won't cover it.

*His right hand and His holy arm.* Not an army. Not a general. *His own arm.* Isaiah 52 — *the Lord has bared His holy arm in the sight of all the nations.* He rolled up His sleeve and did it Himself.

**"The Lord has made His salvation known — and revealed His right-standing to the nations."**

*Made known. Revealed.* Past tense. Not "will someday." *Has.* Psalm 97 — *all peoples see His glory*. Here it's *done*. The nations know.

**"He has remembered His loyal-love and His faithfulness to Israel."**

*Remembered.* Psalm 89 asked *where is Your loyal-love?* Psalm 98 answers: *He remembered it.* Psalm 78 — the people forgot, *He remembered*. The word that saves everything.

**"All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God."**

*All the ends.* The far edges. Psalm 97's distant islands. *Have seen.* Not heard about — *seen*. Luke 2 — *all flesh shall see the salvation of God.* Simeon holding the baby — *my eyes have seen Your salvation.* He was quoting *this*.

Now — the noise. And it escalates:

**"Shout for joy to the Lord, all the earth! Burst into jubilant song with music!"**

*Burst.* The Hebrew is *pitzchu* — break out, break forth. Like a dam. Like something that's been held in and *can't* be anymore.

**"Make music to the Lord with the harp — with the harp and the sound of singing — with trumpets and the blast of the ram's horn — shout for joy before the Lord, the King!"**

Harp. Voices. Trumpets. Ram's horn. Every instrument they had. *The King.* Psalm 93, 96, 97 — enthronement. The coronation band's playing.

And then — creation joins. Psalm 96 gave the trees a part. Psalm 98 gives it to the *water*:

**"Let the sea resound — and everything in it! The world — and all who live in it!"**

**"Let the rivers clap their hands! Let the mountains sing together for joy!"**

*The rivers clap their hands.*

Picture it. Every river on earth — the Nile, the Jordan, the Euphrates, the one behind your house — *applauding*. The Hebrew is *yimcha'u-kaf* — strike the palm. The water hitting the banks, the rapids over rocks — that sound *is* the clapping. It always was. You just didn't know what it was for.

*The mountains sing together.* Psalm 97 melted them like wax. Psalm 98 has them in a *choir*. Same mountains. When the King comes — what was terrifying becomes *harmony*.

**"— before the Lord — because He comes to judge the earth."**

*He comes to judge.* Psalm 96's ending. And the rivers are *clapping* about it. Because *judgment* — in this psalm — isn't the bad news. It's the *good* news. The crooked courts get fixed. The widow gets heard. Psalm 82's failed gods get replaced by the real Judge — and *creation applauds*.

**"He will judge the world in right-standing — and the peoples with equity."**

*Equity.* Straight. Fair. The last word.

Nine verses. Here's the shape: *New song — He did it with His own arm. He REMEMBERED. All the ends of the earth have SEEN it. Burst — harp, trumpet, horn — for the King. Sea, roar. Rivers, CLAP. Mountains, sing. He's coming to set it straight.*

*Joy to the world — the Lord is come. Let earth receive her King.* Watts had it right. *Let every heart prepare Him room — and heaven and nature sing.*

Heaven and *nature*. The rivers already know. Clap with them.
psalms.notes: *Note on translation: v. 1 —* nifla'ot *= wonders, marvelous things;* z'ro'a kodsho *= His holy arm (Isa 52:10, 53:1). v. 2 —* hodia YHWH y'shuato *= "YHWH has made known His salvation." v. 3 —* zachar *= He remembered — answer to Ps 89:49. v. 3 —* ra'u kol-afsei-aretz *= "all ends of the earth have seen" — cf. Luke 2:30–31, 3:6. v. 4 —* pitzchu *= break forth. v. 8 —* n'harot yimcha'u-kaf *= "rivers clap palm";* harim yachad y'ran'nu *= mountains together sing for joy. v. 9 —* b'meisharim *= with equity/uprightness. Basis of Isaac Watts' "Joy to the World" (1719). No* yirah*.*

psalms.title: PSALM 99 — Holy, Holy, Holy
psalms.body:
Psalms 93–98 built the throne. Psalm 99 tells you what the King is *like*. One word. Three times.

**"The Lord reigns! Let the nations tremble! He sits enthroned between the cherubim. Let the earth shake!"**

*The Lord reigns.* Fourth time in Book Four. *Between the cherubim* — the Ark. The mercy seat. The place in the Holy of Holies where the wings met over the box — *that's* the throne. Not a golden chair in a palace. The lid of the Ark, in the dark, once a year.

*Tremble. Shake.* Not fear — *movement*. The reaction of everything to the presence of Something that big.

**"Great is the Lord in Zion. He is exalted over all the nations."**

**"Let them praise Your great and awesome name —**
**He is holy."**

*Awesome.* *Nora.* *Yirah.* Once more — in a verse about *praising*.

*He is holy.* First time. *Kadosh.* Set apart. Other. Not like anything else. The word Isaiah heard the angels shouting — *holy, holy, holy* — Isaiah 6. Psalm 99 has the same *three*.

Now — what holiness *does*:

**"The King is mighty — He loves justice. You have established equity. In Jacob You have done what is just and right."**

*He loves justice.* Not enforces — *loves*. Psalm 33 — *He loves right-standing and justice.* Psalm 37 — *the Lord loves justice.* The holiness isn't distant. It's *passionate about fairness*. That's what "set apart" means here — set apart *from* the crooked scale.

**"Exalt the Lord our God. Worship at His footstool —**
**He is holy."**

*His footstool.* The Ark again — 1 Chronicles 28:2. The earth as the place His feet rest. You're not at the throne. You're at the *footstool*. Close enough to touch what He stands on.

*He is holy.* Second time.

And now — the psalm does something the other enthronement psalms don't. It gets *personal*. Names:

**"Moses and Aaron were among His priests. Samuel was among those who called on His name. They called on the Lord — and He answered them."**

*Moses. Aaron. Samuel.* Three men who *talked to God*. Moses at the bush, on the mountain, face to face. Aaron in the Holy of Holies. Samuel as a boy — *speak, for Your servant is listening*.

*They called — He answered.* That's the pattern. The holy God — the one who makes the earth shake — *answers* when you call. Holiness didn't make Him unreachable. It made Him *reliable*.

**"He spoke to them from the pillar of cloud. They kept His statutes and the decrees He gave them."**

*From the pillar of cloud.* Exodus 13 — the cloud that led them. God *spoke* from it. The same cloud Psalm 97 wrapped around the throne — it *talks*.

**"Lord our God — You answered them. You were to Israel a forgiving God — though You punished their misdeeds."**

*A forgiving God — though You punished.* Both. The Hebrew is *El nose* — a God who *carries* — Psalm 25's *nasa*, Psalm 32's *lifted off*. God who *bears* the sin. And *also* God who *disciplines*. Psalm 89:32–33 — *I'll punish with the rod — but I won't take My love.* Psalm 94 — *happy is the one You discipline*. Forgiveness *and* correction — that's holiness in practice. Not one or the other.

**"Exalt the Lord our God. Worship at His holy mountain —**
**because the Lord our God is holy."**

*He is holy.* Third time. The last words.

Three *holys*. Isaiah's seraphim. Revelation 4 — *holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty*. Psalm 99 is the earliest version — the Ark, the footstool, the mountain — and three men who called and got *answered*.

Nine verses. Here's the shape: *The Lord reigns — from the mercy seat. His name is awesome — He is holy. He LOVES justice — worship at His footstool — He is holy. Moses, Aaron, Samuel — they called, He ANSWERED. He spoke from the cloud. He forgave — and corrected. He is holy.*

Here's what "holy" means in this psalm: *not too high to answer.* The One the earth shakes before is the One who picked up when Moses called. Set apart — *and* on the line.

Call. He's holy. That's *why* He answers.
psalms.notes: *Note on translation: v. 1 —* YHWH malach *= "YHWH reigns" (cf. 93:1, 96:10, 97:1);* yoshev k'ruvim *= sitting [between/on] the cherubim — the Ark (Exod 25:22). v. 3 —* nora *=* yirah *= awesome;* kadosh hu *= "holy [is] He" — refrain at v. 3, 5, 9. v. 4 —* mishpat ahev *= "justice He loves." v. 5 —* hadom raglav *= His footstool (1 Chr 28:2; Isa 66:1). v. 6 —* korim el-YHWH v'hu ya'anem *= "calling to YHWH and He would answer them." v. 8 —* El nose *= a carrying/forgiving God (*nasa*);* nokem al-alilotam *= avenging/punishing their deeds. Threefold* kadosh *— cf. Isa 6:3, Rev 4:8.*

psalms.title: PSALM 100 — Enter His Gates with Thanksgiving
psalms.body:
Psalms 93–99 built the throne, seated the King, called the nations, got the rivers clapping. Psalm 100 is the *walk-in*. Five verses. Seven commands. Here's how you enter.

**"Shout for joy to the Lord — all the earth!"**

Command one. *Shout.* The Hebrew is *hari'u* — the battle cry, the coronation roar. Psalm 47's word. *All the earth* — the whole planet's in the courtyard.

**"Worship the Lord with gladness. Come before Him with joyful songs."**

Commands two and three. *Worship — with GLADNESS.* Not duty. Not dread. *Simchah* — joy. The Hebrew for "worship" here is *ivdu* — *serve*. Serve Him *gladly*. The work is a party.

*Come before Him.* Command three. *Bo'u* — enter. Walk in. Psalm 95 — *come, let us*. You're at the gate.

Now — the reason. And it's the center of the psalm:

**"Know that the Lord is God. It is He who made us — and we are His. We are His people — the sheep of His pasture."**

*Know.* Command four. *Da'u* — know it. Not feel it. *Know*. Psalm 46 — *be still and know*. This is the *knowing* part.

*He made us — and we are His.* Two facts. *Made.* *His.* You didn't make yourself. You don't own yourself. That's not a burden — it's *relief*. The One who made you is the One who keeps you. Psalm 95 — *our Maker*. Psalm 100 — *and we are His*.

*Sheep of His pasture.* One last time. Psalm 23, 74, 79, 80, 95 — *sheep*. The whole book of Psalms is a flock walking home.

And then — the gate:

**"Enter His gates with thanksgiving — and His courts with praise."**

Command five. *Enter.* Psalm 24 — *lift up your heads, you gates*. Psalm 84 — *I'd rather hold the door*. Psalm 87 — *He loves the gates*. Here you *go through*.

*With thanksgiving.* That's the ticket. Not perfection. Not a clean record. *Todah* — thanks. Psalm 50 — *offer God thanksgiving*. Psalm 95 — *come before Him with thanksgiving*. It's the one thing you're asked to bring. You walk in *saying thank you*.

**"Give thanks to Him. Praise His name."**

Commands six and seven. *Thank. Praise.* Once you're inside — that's the whole job.

And the last verse — *why*:

**"Because the Lord is good. His loyal-love endures forever. His faithfulness continues through all generations."**

*Good.* *Tov.* Psalm 92 — *it is good to praise*. Psalm 34 — *taste and see that He is good*. Psalm 73 — *it is good to be near God*. The word that started creation — *and God saw that it was good* — is the reason you walk through the gate.

*Loyal-love forever.* *Chesed l'olam.* The refrain that Psalm 136 will repeat twenty-six times. The thing Psalm 89 thought was lost. *Forever.*

*Faithfulness through all generations.* *Emunah.* Psalm 89's seven. Psalm 78's chain — fathers to children to children yet unborn. The faithfulness *outlasts* you. It was here before you and it'll be here after — and you got to walk through the gate in the middle of it.

Five verses. Seven commands. Here's the shape: *Shout. Serve gladly. Come in. KNOW — He made you, you're His, you're the sheep. Enter the gate with THANKS. Thank Him. Praise His name. Because He's good — loyal-love forever — faithfulness to every generation.*

One hundred psalms. Two-thirds of the way. Book One's two roads. Book Two's deer panting. Book Three's throne in the dirt. Book Four's *the Lord reigns*. And now — the gate.

Here's how you walk through it: *thank you*. That's the whole password. Say it and go in.
psalms.notes: *Note on translation: heading —* mizmor l'todah *= "a psalm for thanksgiving/the thank-offering" — unique. v. 1 —* hari'u *= shout (cf. 47:1, 98:4). v. 2 —* ivdu et-YHWH b'simchah *= "serve YHWH with gladness." v. 3 —* d'u *= know;* hu asanu v'lo anachnu *= "He made us and His we are" (Ketiv reads* v'lo *"and not we [ourselves]"; Qere reads* v'lo *"and to Him [we belong]" — both true, the Qere is followed). v. 4 —* b'todah *= with thanksgiving;* bit'hillah *= with praise. v. 5 —* ki-tov YHWH *= "for good [is] YHWH";* l'olam chasdo *= forever His loyal-love;* ad-dor va-dor emunato *= to generation and generation His faithfulness. No* yirah*.*

psalms.title: PSALM 101 — I Will Not Set Before My Eyes
psalms.body:
After the enthronement psalms — a human king sitting down to decide how *he'll* rule under the real King. This is the job interview.

**"I will sing of Your loyal-love and justice. To You, Lord, I will sing praise."**

*Loyal-love and justice.* The two things Psalm 89 and 99 said hold up God's throne. David wants them holding up *his*.

**"I will be careful to lead a blameless life. When will You come to me?"**

*When will You come to me?* A question in the middle of the resolutions. He's saying: *I'll clean the house — and I'm waiting for the guest.* The whole psalm is getting ready for a visit.

Now — the resolutions. And the first one is about *himself*:

**"I will conduct the affairs of my house with a blameless heart."**

*My house.* Start there. Not the kingdom. Not the courts. *Home.* The place nobody sees. If it's not straight there, it's not straight anywhere.

**"I will not set before my eyes anything that is worthless."**

*Before my eyes.* The screen. The feed. The thing you stare at when nobody's watching. David's deciding what gets to be *in front of him*. Not what he does — what he *looks at*. Because what's in front of the eyes ends up in the heart. Psalm 119 will say *turn my eyes from worthless things*. Here it's a *decision*.

The Hebrew is *d'var b'liya'al* — a *worthless* thing. Belial. The stuff that's *nothing* dressed up as something. He won't look at it.

**"I hate what faithless people do. I will have no part in it."**

*No part.* Not "I'll be careful around it." *Zero.*

**"The perverse of heart shall be far from me. I will have nothing to do with what is evil."**

*Far from me.* Distance. Psalm 1 — *don't walk with them, don't sit with them.* Psalm 26 — *I don't sit with the hidden ones.* He's choosing his *radius*.

Now — the house staff:

**"Whoever slanders their neighbor in secret — I will put to silence. Whoever has haughty eyes and a proud heart — I will not tolerate."**

*Slanders in secret.* Psalm 15 — *doesn't pick up a reproach against his friend.* The whisperer doesn't get a seat at David's table.

*Haughty eyes.* The look-down. The one who's already decided he's above the room. *Not tolerated.* Not because pride's a sin in a list — because a proud man *can't serve*. He's too busy being served.

**"My eyes will be on the faithful in the land — that they may dwell with me. The one whose walk is blameless will minister to me."**

*My eyes will be on.* Verse 3 — *I won't set worthless things before my eyes.* Verse 6 — *my eyes will be on the faithful.* He's not just *removing* — he's *replacing*. Take the trash out of the line of sight. Put *faithful people* there instead.

*They may dwell with me.* Live in the house. The faithful get *proximity*. That's the reward for integrity in this psalm — not money, not rank. *Closeness to the king.*

**"No one who practices deceit will dwell in my house. No one who speaks falsely will stand in my presence."**

*Speaks falsely.* Psalm 12's smooth lips. Psalm 52's razor tongue. Psalm 55's butter-smooth betrayer. David's been *burned* by every one of these. Now he's king — and the liar doesn't get past the door.

And the last verse:

**"Every morning I will put to silence all the wicked in the land. I will cut off every evildoer from the city of the Lord."**

*Every morning.* Daily. Not a one-time purge. A *routine*. Every dawn — check the house, check the court, check who's whispering. The Hebrew is *la-b'karim* — *in the mornings*. Plural. It never stops.

Eight verses. Seven *I wills*. Here's the shape: *I'll sing of loyal-love and justice. Start with my own house. Nothing worthless in front of my eyes. Nothing to do with the crooked. No slanderers, no proud eyes. My eyes on the FAITHFUL — they live with me. No liars past the door. Every morning — clean it again.*

Here's what to do with it: you've got a house. Maybe not a kingdom — but a house. What's in front of your eyes? Who's at your table? Who whispers in your ear? David made a list. Make one.

And ask his question: *when will You come to me?* Then get the house ready.
psalms.notes: *Note on translation: v. 2 —* matai tavo elai *= "when will You come to me?" v. 3 —* lo-asit l'neged einai d'var-b'liya'al *= "I will not set before my eyes a worthless thing" —* b'liya'al *= worthlessness, Belial. v. 5 —* m'lashni ba-seter *= slanderer in secret;* g'vah-einayim *= high/haughty of eyes. v. 6 —* einai b'ne'emnei-eretz *= "my eyes [are] on the faithful of the land." v. 7 —* dover sh'karim *= speaker of lies. v. 8 —* la-b'karim *= in the mornings (plural). No* yirah*.*

psalms.title: PSALM 102 — But You Remain the Same
psalms.body:
The heading tells you everything: *an afflicted person who has grown weak.* Not a king. Not a prophet. Just someone worn down — pouring it out.

**"Hear my prayer, Lord. Let my cry for help come to You. Don't hide Your face from me when I'm in distress. Turn Your ear to me. When I call — answer me quickly."**

*Quickly.* Psalm 70's *hurry*. He doesn't have time for slow.

Now — the body. And it's Psalm 38's honesty:

**"My days vanish like smoke. My bones burn like glowing embers. My heart is blighted and withered like grass. I forget to eat my food."**

*I forget to eat.* Not "I can't eat." *Forget.* The body's needs stop registering. If you've been in depression — you know. The meals just don't happen.

**"In my distress I groan aloud — and am reduced to skin and bones."**

**"I am like a desert owl — like an owl among the ruins. I lie awake. I have become like a bird alone on a roof."**

Three birds. *Desert owl* — in the empty places. *Owl in the ruins* — Psalm 74's rubble. *A bird alone on a roof* — the sparrow that *didn't* find the nest by the altar. Psalm 84 envied the bird that got in. Psalm 102 is the bird that didn't.

*I lie awake.* Psalm 77's insomnia. Psalm 63's night watches. Alone. On the roof. Eyes open.

**"All day long my enemies taunt me. Those who rail against me use my name as a curse."**

*Use my name as a curse.* His *name* has become the *insult*. "You're a real ___." That's how far down it's gone.

**"I eat ashes as my food — and mingle my drink with tears."**

*Ashes for food.* Psalm 42's tears as bread — now it's ashes. What you eat when there's nothing left.

**"— because of Your great wrath. You have taken me up and thrown me aside."**

*Thrown me aside.* Picked up — and tossed. Like something you don't need.

**"My days are like the evening shadow. I wither away like grass."**

*Evening shadow.* Long and thin and about to disappear into the dark. *Grass.* Psalm 90, 92, 103 — the grass again. He's *dying*, and he knows it.

Eleven verses of that. And then — verse 12. The word that changes every lament:

**"But You, Lord — sit enthroned forever. Your renown endures through all generations."**

*But You.* Not *but I* — that was David's. This one's *but YOU*. The afflicted man doesn't have a *but I*. He's got nothing. So he turns the whole sentence around and puts *God* in the subject position. *I'm smoke. YOU'RE forever.*

**"You will arise and have compassion on Zion — because it is time to show favor to her. The appointed time has come."**

*The appointed time.* Psalm 75 — *when I choose the time*. The afflicted man says: *it's HERE.* Not because he feels it. Because he's decided to *say* it.

**"Because her stones are dear to Your servants. Her very dust moves them to pity."**

*Her dust.* The rubble of Jerusalem. Psalm 74, 79. And the exiles *love the dust*. They'd kiss the ground if they could get to it. That's what it means to belong to a place — you love it broken.

**"The nations will stand in awe of the name of the Lord. All the kings of the earth will revere Your glory. Because the Lord will rebuild Zion — and appear in His glory."**

*Rebuild.* Not "restore the mood." *Rebuild the stones.* Psalm 51 — *build the walls of Jerusalem*. It's a *construction* promise.

*Stand in awe.* *Yirah.* The nations — in wonder.

**"He will respond to the prayer of the destitute. He will not despise their plea."**

*Not despise.* Psalm 22, 51, 69 — the broken thing He won't turn away from.

**"Let this be written for a future generation — that a people not yet created may praise the Lord."**

*A people not yet created.* He's writing for *you*. Sitting on the roof, forgetting to eat, eating ashes — and he says *write this down for the people who don't exist yet.* Psalm 22's *a people not yet born*. Psalm 78's chain. The afflicted man knows his suffering is *material* for someone he'll never meet.

**"'The Lord looked down from His sanctuary on high — from heaven He viewed the earth — to hear the groans of the prisoners — and release those condemned to death.'"**

*The groans of the prisoners.* Psalm 79. He *heard* them. And *released*.

**"So the name of the Lord will be declared in Zion — and His praise in Jerusalem — when the peoples and the kingdoms assemble to worship the Lord."**

Psalm 87 — the nations *inside*.

Now — back to the man. And it's brutal for one more verse:

**"In the course of my life He broke my strength. He cut short my days."**

*Cut short.* He's not going to get his seventy.

**"So I said: 'Don't take me away, my God, in the midst of my days —'"**

And then — the turn *out of himself* entirely. The last six verses. Hebrews 1 quotes them about Christ:

**"'— Your years go on through all generations. In the beginning You laid the foundations of the earth — and the heavens are the work of Your hands.'"**

*In the beginning.* Genesis 1. The man who's dying goes back to the *first* thing.

**"'They will perish — but You remain. They will all wear out like a garment. Like clothing You will change them — and they will be discarded.'"**

*They will wear out.* The *heavens*. The *earth*. The oldest, most permanent things anyone can see — *clothes*. Getting threadbare. Going in the bin. God *changes them* like a shirt.

Think about what he's doing. He started with *my days vanish like smoke*. He ends with *the universe wears out like a garment*. He's put his own dying in the *same category* as the stars burning out. Everything's temporary. *Everything.* The heavens *and* him.

**"'But You remain the same — and Your years will never end.'"**

*But You.* Second time. *The same.* The Hebrew is *atah-hu* — *You are He.* Unchanging. The one fixed point in a universe that's wearing out.

Hebrews 1:10–12 quotes this — about *Jesus*. *You, Lord, laid the foundations of the earth... they will perish, but You remain... You are the same.* The dying man on the roof was describing the Son.

**"'The children of Your servants will live in Your presence. Their descendants will be established before You.'"**

*Their descendants — established.* The man won't get his seventy. But his *kids* — Psalm 90's *establish the work of our hands* — they'll be *in the presence*. The line goes on. His doesn't. Theirs does. And that's enough for him to stop asking.

Twenty-eight verses. Here's the shape: *I'm smoke. I forget to eat. I'm a bird alone on a roof. Ashes for food. You threw me aside. — BUT YOU sit enthroned forever. It's time to rebuild Zion. Write this down for people not born yet. — He cut my days short. — But You laid the foundations. The heavens will wear out like a shirt. You'll fold them up. But YOU remain the same. And the kids will be established.*

You're smoke? So are the stars. And there's One who isn't. Put *Him* in the subject position and see what happens to the sentence.
psalms.notes: *Note on translation: heading —* t'fillah l'ani chi-ya'atof *= "a prayer of an afflicted one when he grows faint." v. 4 —* shachachti me-achol lachmi *= "I forgot to eat my bread." v. 6 —* k'at midbar *= like a desert owl/pelican;* k'kos choravot *= like an owl of ruins. v. 7 —* k'tzipor boded al-gag *= "like a bird alone on a roof." v. 9 —* efer ka-lechem *= ashes like bread. v. 12 —* v'atah YHWH l'olam teshev *= "but You, YHWH, forever sit [enthroned]." v. 15 —* v'yir'u *=* yirah *= will stand in awe. v. 18 —* am nivra *= a people [to be] created. v. 25–27 — quoted in Hebrews 1:10–12 of Christ. v. 27 —* v'atah-hu *= "but You [are] He" — unchanging.*

psalms.title: PSALM 103 — Bless the Lord, O My Soul
psalms.body:
Psalm 102 was the man on the roof. Psalm 103 is what you sing when you've come down.

**"Bless the Lord, O my soul. All my inmost being — bless His holy name."**

*O my soul.* David's talking to *himself*. Psalm 42's technique — *why are you downcast, my soul?* But now it's not a question. It's an *order*. *Soul — bless Him.* He's commanding the deepest part of himself to get up and praise.

*All my inmost being.* The Hebrew is *kol-k'ravai* — all my insides. Organs. Guts. The part that doesn't have words. *That* part — bless.
